gaps.sentence: The training course will ___ you to work abroad (QUALIFY).
gaps.explanation: The suffix -ify forms the verb: qualify. A base verb follows 'will'.

gaps.sentence: New technology has ___ the way we work (REVOLUTION).
gaps.explanation: The suffix -ise forms the verb: revolutionise. After 'has' the past participle 'revolutionised' is needed.

gaps.sentence: Her kindness and ___ (GENEROUS) made her very popular.
gaps.explanation: Parallel to 'kindness', a noun is needed: generosity (note the irregular -osity spelling).

gaps.sentence: Their ___ was celebrated with a big party (MARRY).
gaps.hint: noun needed after 'Their'; note the spelling change
gaps.explanation: The noun of 'marry' is 'marriage' (-age); an adjective cannot follow 'Their' as subject.

gaps.sentence: The treaty will strengthen economic ___ between the two countries (COOPERATE).
gaps.explanation: An adjective is followed by a noun: cooperation (-tion noun).

gaps.sentence: His sudden ___ came as a shock to everyone (DEPART).
gaps.hint: noun needed as subject (-ure); beware the word meaning 'part of an organisation'
gaps.explanation: The noun of 'depart' is departure (-ure); a department is a section of an organisation.

gaps.sentence: The meeting has been ___ until Thursday (SCHEDULE).
gaps.hint: arranged for a new time (re-); past participle needed
gaps.explanation: The prefix re- means again/afresh: rescheduled means given a new time. The passive needs the past participle.

gaps.sentence: The team played ___ and deserved to win (EXCELLENT).
gaps.explanation: An adverb modifies the verb 'played': excellently (-ly).
